lines.trans: Chef, forgive me, please!
I have never seen truffles before.
How could you throw away such a treasure?
In Voronezh, truffles are only candies!
Candies? This is the most expensive mushroom!
I thought that they had spoiled.
Good thing the homeless man returned them to us.

words.gloss: to give back, to get back

lines.trans: Alright, I am very kind today.
We successfully passed the difficult inspection.

words.gloss: to go through, to pass; to come along

lines.trans: But you will pay the bill for his dinner.
Twenty-two thousand roubles?!
This is how you will remember this lesson!

meanings.note: masculine animate (substantivized adjective)

examples.text: Хорошо, что бездомный вернул их нам.
examples.trans: Good thing the homeless man returned them to us.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

вернуть.gloss: to give back, to get back

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to give back', forming an aspectual pair with 'возвращать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to get back') (money you spent) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ты эти деньги через полгода вернёшь.
examples.trans: You'll get this money back in six months.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to see', forming an aspectual pair with 'увидеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = see?') (drawing attention) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

examples.text: Ты видишь, сколько гостей сегодня вечером сидит в зале?
examples.trans: Do you see how many guests are sitting in the hall tonight?

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('here') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('! = you'll see!') (emphasis) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: выбросить в окно = to throw out the window

examples.trans: He threw the mayor out the window.

examples.text: Он мэра в окно выбросил. Вы помните?
examples.trans: He threw the mayor out the window. Do you remember?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'mushroom' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

meanings.note: 'два' with masculine/neuter nouns, 'две' with feminine; the noun goes into the genitive singular

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: followed by genitive plural in nominative/accusative

examples.text: Я уже вам сто раз говорила. Я брала двадцать тысяч, вернула тридцать!
examples.trans: I've already told you a hundred times. I borrowed twenty thousand, paid back thirty!

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'kind', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.
in greetings: добрый день, добрый вечер

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: to a loved one, and at the start of letters
to a loved one, and at the start of letters

examples.text: В Москве вам дают деньги на дорогую одежду, а мозги не дают.
examples.trans: In Moscow they give you money for expensive clothes, but they don't give you brains.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('behind') (+ instrumental) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'помнить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to remember', forming an aspectual pair with 'запоминать'.

examples.text: Вот так на митингах говори, запомни.
examples.trans: That's how you talk at rallies, remember that.

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to excuse', forming an aspectual pair with 'извинять'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to excuse, to forgive') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Thank you, Marina. Sorry, I'm in a hurry.

meanings.en: to spoil, go bad, deteriorate (of food or things)
meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'портиться'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to spoil'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.trans: I thought that the groceries had spoiled.
I thought that they had spoiled.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'how'.
Secondary conversational sense ('as') (как вы знаете = as you know) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'sweet, piece of candy' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Here, I bought some sweets for the kids.

examples.text: Вот детям конфет купил. А семья и без меня хорошо время проводит!
examples.trans: Here, I bought sweets for the kids. And the family is having a good time without me!

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('all right') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'can', forming an aspectual pair with 'смочь'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
used with не before the verb, or alone

examples.text: Я никогда не был на море.
examples.trans: I've never been to the sea.

examples.text: Я никогда в жизни не пробовал такой вкусной утки!
examples.trans: I have never in my life tasted such delicious duck!

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'but', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

оказаться.gloss: to turn out to be, find oneself

meanings.en: to turn out to be, prove to be
meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to turn out to be', forming an aspectual pair with 'оказываться'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.trans: You turned out to be ungrateful.

examples.text: Он внезапно оказался в центре событий.
examples.trans: He suddenly found himself in the center of events.
And you turned out to be an ungrateful woman!

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
Secondary conversational sense ('it') (for masculine and neuter things) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
High-frequency Russian pronoun ('they') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.en: to pay for, to pay off (+ accusative)
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to pay, to pay off', paired with 'оплачивать'.

examples.text: Послушай, я оплачу весь долг этой женщины!
examples.trans: Listen, I'll pay this woman's entire debt!

examples.text: Он уже оплатил счёт в ресторане.
examples.trans: He has already paid the bill at the restaurant.

examples.text: Послушай, я оплачу весь долг этой женщины! Клянусь, весь долг!
examples.trans: Listen, I'll pay this woman's entire debt! I swear, the whole debt!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: to think it over, to give it a thought
meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'умать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to think', forming an aspectual pair with 'думать'.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('please') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('you're welcome') (answer to thanks) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('here you are') (handing something over) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

meanings.en: garbage dump, dumpster, dustbin, rubbish heap
meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'garbage dump'.

examples.trans: Rare mushrooms ended up in the dumpster.
Take the bag to the trash dump.

examples.text: Ладно, я отнесу её на помойку.
examples.trans: Okay, I will take it to the dumpster.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'why'.

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'верка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'check, inspection, test' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: An inspection is underway at the bank.

examples.text: Эксперты уже начали проверку состояния старой стены.
examples.trans: Experts have already begun checking the condition of the old wall.

пройти.gloss: to go through, to pass; to come along

meanings.note: about a feeling or pain: потом пройдёт = it'll pass
'Пройдёмте' = let's go, an official's polite order

examples.text: Пройдёмте, пожалуйста, за мной к вашему столику у окна.
examples.trans: Please come along with me to your table by the window.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'earlier'.

examples.text: В моей комнате раньше дядя Миша жил.
examples.trans: Uncle Misha used to live in my room.
There used to be an old park here.

examples.text: Подождите. В моей комнате раньше дядя Миша жил.
examples.trans: Wait. Uncle Misha used to live in my room.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'rare', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: У меня есть много редких материалов.
Макс, почему редкие трюфели оказались на помойке?
examples.trans: Max, why did rare truffles end up in the dumpster?

examples.text: Но вы обязаны распробовать этот редкий шедевр!
examples.trans: But you must taste this rare masterpiece!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'rouble', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: I haven't got a single rouble.

examples.text: Наша задача — взять у взяточников миллиард рублей.
examples.trans: Our task is to take a billion roubles from the bribe-takers.

meanings.note: forms the superlative: самый главный = the most important
Secondary conversational sense ('the very') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
Do you know the main thing?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'today'.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ложный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('complicated, difficult').

examples.trans: Danila, let's go. Look, there's nothing complicated.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'treasure', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Как ты мог выбросить такое сокровище?
examples.trans: How could you throw away such a treasure?

examples.text: Как ты вообще мог выбросить в мусор такое сокровище?
examples.trans: How could you possibly throw such a treasure into the trash?

examples.text: Этот старинный медный сотейник — настоящее сокровище нашей кухни.
examples.trans: This vintage copper saucepan is a true treasure of our kitchen.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'account', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('bill, check') (in a restaurant) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Или счёт в банке. Потому что они все обманщики.
examples.trans: Or a bank account. Because they are all cheats.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('so') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('like that, so') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Secondary conversational sense ('? = what's this?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry
Declinable masculine noun meaning 'truffle', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: В Воронеже трюфели — это только конфеты.
examples.trans: In Voronezh, truffles are only chocolate candies.

examples.text: Шеф, дорогой, а трюфели тебе надо?
examples.trans: Chef, my dear, do you need truffles?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: the noun after it is genitive plural: тысячи мест

examples.text: Мы построим кластер. Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: We will build the cluster. That means thousands of jobs.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'dinner, supper (evening meal)' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Что у нас сегодня на ужин?
examples.trans: What do we have for dinner today?

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: in уроки учить / делать уроки, plural
in уроки учить / делать уроки, plural

examples.trans: Not allowed? All right, I'll go and do my homework.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'successfully'.

examples.text: Я надеюсь, что мы успешно сработаемся.
examples.trans: I hope that we will work well together.
We will surely successfully pass the inspection.
We successfully passed the difficult inspection.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'well'.
Secondary conversational sense ('good, fine') (as an answer) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Хорошо, Виктор Петрович, я сейчас же всё переделаю заново!
examples.trans: All right, Viktor Petrovich, I will redo everything right now!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
